name: Tool use & protocols (MCP)
summary: Letting a model call functions and services through structured requests, standardised by protocols such as MCP.

text: On its own an AI can only talk. Giving it tools is like giving it a phone and a calculator: now it can check the weather or do exact maths.
It asks in a special format, and a program does the actual work.
D1.analogy: Handing someone a phone and a calculator.

text: Developers describe each tool with a name, a description and a schema for its arguments.
When a tool would help, the model outputs a structured **tool call** instead of prose; the application runs the tool and returns the result to the model.
Protocols such as the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** standardise how tools and data sources are offered to AI applications, so one integration works across many clients.
D2.analogy: Handing someone a phone and a calculator.
D2.analogyBreaks: A person decides whether to believe what they hear on the phone. Models tend to treat tool results as trustworthy, so malicious text inside a result can steer them (prompt injection).

predict.question: Who actually runs a tool call?
options: The application or client that receives the call
predict.explanation: The model only produces a structured request; the surrounding application decides whether and how to run it, which is also where permissions belong.

text: Open problems: securing tool ecosystems against poisoned tools and over-broad permissions, authentication for remote tools, and agents discovering tools on the fly.

sources.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
